name: PagerDuty/cronner
description: cron job runner; statsd metrics with optional DogStatsd event emissions
why: A focused, single-purpose ops utility (cron wrapper with statsd/DogStatsd event emission) archived by PagerDuty in favor of a community fork (theckman/cronner) -- a clean example of a corporate tool handed off to the community rather than truly abandoned, and small enough to actually read end to end.

name: CartoDB/labs-postgresql
description: PostgreSQL workshop covering lesser-known features (psql tricks, PostGIS, expression indexes, full-text search, PL/Python, declarative partitioning, TOAST) delivered at CommitConf 2018
why: A corporate-sponsored (CARTO) conference workshop repo, self-archived as historical reference -- the same 'workshop/teaching material, not a product' pattern as django-deployment-workshop already in this dataset, but for PostgreSQL/PostGIS. No license file present, so cataloged as metadata-only; nothing referenced or copied.

name: RedpointArchive/Protogame
description: A powerful cross-platform game engine for C#, built on MonoGame
why: A full-featured, production-grade cross-platform C# game engine (2D/3D, deferred rendering, multiplayer networking, physics, in-game console) that its own maintainers deliberately sunset in a public announcement rather than letting it silently rot -- the first genuinely game/creative-shaped entry in a dataset that has so far been entirely ops tooling, libraries, bots, and teaching workshops.
pushed_at_note: pushed_at is the GitHub-reported archive date (repository was archived by the owner on Mar 6, 2018); exact last-commit date not independently confirmed.

name: dmarx/psaw
description: Python Pushshift.io API Wrapper (for comment/submission search)
why: A minimalist client for pulling historical Reddit comment/submission data out of the (now largely defunct) Pushshift dataset -- the dataset's first genuinely dataset/data-access-shaped entry (previously 8/8 entries were ops tooling, libraries, bots, workshops, or a game engine). The README's own maintainer marked it 'STALE' and pointed users to a maintained fork (PMAW) rather than leaving it to silently rot -- the same self-aware sunset pattern as redpoint-protogame.
pushed_at_note: pushed_at is the GitHub-reported archive date (repository was archived by the owner on Feb 7, 2024); exact last-commit date not independently confirmed (commit history page is client-rendered and returned empty via this sandbox's fetch tool, same limitation noted for redpoint-protogame in run 5).

name: googlecreativelab/teachable-machine-v1
description: Explore how machine learning works, live in the browser. No coding required.
why: A browser-based creative ML experiment from Google Creative Lab (built with friends from Stoj, Use All Five, and PAIR) that let anyone train an image classifier live with a webcam, no code required -- the dataset's first purely creative non-game system (previously 9/9 entries were ops tooling, libraries, a bot, workshops, a game engine, or a dataset-access tool). Sunset deliberately rather than abandoned: the repo is literally named 'v1', its README points users to a boilerplate spin-off (teachable-machine-boilerplate) and the live successor at g.co/teachablemachine -- the same self-aware-sunset pattern as redpoint-protogame, dmarx-psaw, and mozilla-notes, now observed in 4 of 10 entries.
stars_note: GitHub's server-rendered page shows the rounded value '3.9k stars' (603 forks); the exact star count is not server-rendered, so 3900 is the rounded figure as displayed, not an exact count.
pushed_at_note: pushed_at is the GitHub-reported archive date (repository was archived by the owner on Mar 19, 2023); exact last-commit date not independently confirmed (commit history page is client-rendered and returns empty via this sandbox's fetch tool, same limitation as redpoint-protogame and dmarx-psaw).
